key_insight: PhySeqNet uses physics-informed synthetic training to detect fluorescent BARseq foci without manual annotation, improving sensitivity in dense tissue images.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical, modular detector for spatial transcriptomics pipelines that can be deployed where real ground truth is unavailable.
method: Trains a U-Net on semi-synthetic images generated from an instrument-matched optical model plus real experimental noise.
Integrates barcode-aware non-maxima suppression (NMSB) to reduce duplicate detections in crowded regions.
Built as part of pyBARseq for end-to-end BARseq analysis.
evidence_signal: On real tissue, reconstruction-based evaluation showed higher fidelity than BarDensr, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning detector, with a median 51 counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr.
watch_item: Performance on real tissue is inferred indirectly through forward-model reconstruction because reliable manual ground truth is unavailable.
paper_title: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
